rationale: Physically motivated harvested-population setup. r=0.6/time unit and K=1000 give a natural population-doubling scale of a few time units and max natural production ~r*K/(4*(1+c/2*1/2)) ~ around 100; harvest_quota=40 sits below that maximum, creating the promised low-abundance threshold separating collapse from recovery to the upper balance. crowding_saturation_strength=0.5 gives mild Beverton-Holt-style saturation of per-capita loss. crowding_relaxation_time=5 lets the ecological load lag behind N by a meaningful fraction of a seasonal period (5). harvest_availability_scale=200 with harvest_encounter_dispersion=2 keeps the saturating harvest-catchability correction on-scale with abundance. seasonal_growth_amplitude=0.15 (within suggested 0.05-0.25) and seasonal_period=5 within the suggested 1-20 range give clearly visible seasonal oscillations of production without ever flipping recruitment negative (|amp|<1). seasonal_phase=0. Initial N=100 sits on the recovery side of the threshold but not near either equilibrium, so the trajectory sweeps through both the recruitment-limited and harvest-limited regimes across t in [0,60] (~12 seasonal cycles, several relaxation times), giving broad excitation across N, crowding_load, and t.
